items.title: Nigeria’s debt interest payments surge 37.5% to N7.7trn in H1’26 — World Bank
items.description: By Yinka Kolawole, with agency report Nigeria’s debt interest payments surged by 37.5 per cent to N7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026 from N5.6 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025. This indicates that the interest payments exceed the Federal Government’s revenue of N6.2 trillion during the period by N1.5 trillion, representing 24.2 per cent. The World Bank disclosed this in its 2026 Nigeria Development Update (NDU), titled ‘Beyond the Federal Purse: How Higher Revenues Reshaped State Priorities’. According to the report, interest payments rose to 3.1 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the first half of 2026, from 2.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, highlighting the growing pressure of debt servicing on public finances. The increase came despite a significant improvement in Federal Government revenue, which rose by more than 72 per cent to N6.2 trillion, representing 2.5 per cent of GDP, from N3.6 trillion, or 1.6 per cent of GDP, in the first half of 2025. The bank attributed the revenue growth to a recovery in oil receipts, stronger corporate tax collections and higher independent revenues, while customs revenues remained stable and Value Added Tax (VAT) collections were comparatively flat. It stated: “Federal revenues rose to about 2.5 per cent of GDP (N6.2 trillion), from 1.6 per cent of GDP (N3.6 trillion) a year earlier, supported by a recovery in oil receipts, stronger corporate tax collections, and higher independent revenues, while customs revenues held stable and VAT collections stayed comparatively flat.” On expenditure, the World Bank said interest payments increased to 3.1 per cent of GDP, or N7.7 trillion, from 2.5 per cent, or N5.6 trillion, amid high domestic borrowing costs. The rising debt burden coincided with a sharp decline in reported capital expenditure, which fell to 0.3 per cent of GDP, or N700 billion, from 1.0 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. Other expenditure remained unchanged at 1.3 per cent of GDP. Meanwhile, total government expenditure rose to N16.1 trillion in the first half of 2026 from N14.6 trillion a year earlier, although it declined marginally as a share of GDP to 6.5 per cent from 6.6 per cent. Personnel costs also increased to N4.2 trillion from N3.7 trillion following wage adjustments, but remained unchanged at 1.7 per cent of GDP. The figures underscore the pressure of rising debt-servicing costs on the Federal Government’s fiscal position, with interest payments exceeding revenue and reported capital spending accounting for a smaller share of economic output. The post Nigeria’s debt interest payments surge 37.5% to N7.7trn in H1’26 — World Bank appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN Futsal 2026 : entrée en matière réussie pour les Lions de l’Atlas face à l’Algérie
items.description: Le Maroc, triple tenant du titre, a parfaitement lancé sa Coupe d’Afrique des Nations de futsal 2026 à Rabat en s’imposant face à son homologue algérien (4-0), confirmant son statut de grand favori de la compétition. Devant des tribunes de la salle Moulay Abdellah de Rabat acquises à leur cause, les hommes de Hicham Dguig n'ont pas tremblé pour leur premier match du Groupe A. Face à un bloc algérien déterminé à créer la surprise, les Lions de l'Atlas ont su faire sauter le verrou adverse grâce à leur fluidité technique et leur expérience des grands rendez-vous africains. Maîtres du ballon dès les premières minutes, les nationaux ont dicté le tempo de la rencontre et inscrit des buts, avec notamment un triplé de Youssef Jaouad. L'ouverture du score précoce (10è – Youness Mkasri) a permis de libérer les espaces, mettant en lumière le génie tactique du sélectionneur national. L'Algérie a bien tenté de réagir en contre-attaque, mais en vain, et la solidité de son gardien lui a permis d'éviter un score plus lourd. Avec cette entame victorieuse, le Maroc prend sereinement les commandes de son destin avant de défier la Zambie et la Libye pour la suite de la phase de poules. Lors de la deuxième journée, mercredi 14 octobre, le Maroc jouera la Zambie (20h00) alors que l'Algérie affronte la Libye (17h00). items.title: Décès du Pr Diamé Signaté : l’université perd un érudit initié aux arcanes de la Linguistique historique
items.description: L’université sénégalaise perd un érudit initié aux arcanes de la Linguistique historique du XVIᵉ et XVIIᵉ siècle, avec le décès du Professeur Diamé Signaté survenu le lundi 12 octobre 2026 à Dakar. Professeur titulaire de classe exceptionnelle, Diamé Signaté est rappelé à Dieu ce lundi à Dakar. Spécialiste de Linguistique française du XVIe et XVIIe siècle, il a fait toute sa carrière de 1981 à sa retraite en 2013 au département de Lettres modernes de la Faculté des Lettres et des Sciences humaines (FLSH) de l’université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar. « Ses enseignements ont été salués par des générations successives pour la rigueur et la clarté de la démarche pédagogique. Il a également contribué à la recherche dans son domaine et mis en place une équipe d'enseignants compétents à l'UCAD et à l'UGB », a témoigné le Professeur Fallou Ndiaye. Avec deux thèses soutenues à la Sorbonne dans les années 80 et 90, le Pr. Signaté a écrit de nombreuses publications académiques dans la discipline aux Presses universitaires de France en particulier. « Signaté était un érudit initié au arcanes de la Linguistique historique du XVIe et XVIIe siècle, formé à la bonne école à une époque où seuls quelques rares Africains s'approchaient de la Grammaire historique (Senghor, Oumar Sankharé, Nguissaly Sarré en particulier », a renchéri le Pr. Ndiaye. A lire aussi : Leadership international en dermatologie : La Pr Fatimata Ly de l’Ucad honorée Au-delà des amphis de l’Ucad, en tant qu’homme politique, le Pr. Diamé Signaté a été engagé dans le Parti socialiste (PS) et était de la même génération que feu Djibo Ka de l'Alliance des forces pour le progrès (AFP) puis le Parti démocratique sénégalais (PDS). Ainsi, il a milité, notamment dans son terroir de Nétéboulou au nord-est de Tambacounda. Ainsi, il défendait avec dévotion ses convictions politiques de militant de l’Union progressiste sénégalaise (UPS) et du PS dans un campus où régnait sans partage l'hégémonie de la pensée marxiste des groupes de gauche et d'extrême gauche. En réalité, le Pr. Signaté avait un sens aigu de la tolérance et de la nuance, hérité certainement du clan des Signaté des deux rives de la Sénégambie, à cheval des terroirs Soninké et Mandingue. Le Pr. Diamé Signaté a été successivement ministre de l'Enseignement technique et de la Formation professionnelle entre 2007 et 2008 sous le président Abdoulaye Wade avant d’être nommé ambassadeur du Sénégal en Gambie de 2009 à 2012. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyberattack
items.description: Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyberattack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50 °C (120°F) overnight, according to one affected supermarket chain. The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the “extremely serious and unprecedented” attack. More than 100 of the chain’s supermarkets were targeted, while 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, with a spokesman saying that another 100 shops were urgently disconnected from the internet to prevent the same thing happening to them. Other major food retailers, including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc, were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by the Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Normally, supermarket freezers undergo a brief overnight defrosting period, during which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports on how warm the fridges and freezers could become in the process. Danfoss said the affected cold units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a risk they had identified. The firm added in s statement that it had “long advised” businesses to keep supported systems up to date. “Reliable refrigeration is critical to our customers’ operations, and we remain committed to supporting our customers and helping them maintain secure and reliable systems they are used to.” The full scale of the attack is unclear, but figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 400 stores were affected out of 15,000 or so overall in France. Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed. In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group – which owns Intermarché and Netto – said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon. The stores had “taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units”, it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves “as soon as possible”. Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported. As a result of the attack, managers arriving at branches of several supermarket chains on Monday morning were hit by a wave of hot air from the freezers. In some places there were even small fires. French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C. Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of €270,000 (£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions. French prosecutors have opened a specific cybercrime investigation into the incident, which the Paris prosecutor’s office described as a “large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France”. European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: “Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality.” In a post on X, Coopérative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were “fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible”. He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was “unacceptable”.

items.title: Tinubu’s re-election crucial to Nigeria’s prosperity – Hamzat
items.description: The Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, says re-election of President Bola Tinubu and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates will be crucial to achieving the prosperity Nigerians desire. Hamzat, who is also the APC governorship candidate in Lagos State for the 2027 general elections, spoke during the inauguration of the PBAT/KOH Lagos Central Campaign Office on Harden Str. Lagos Island on Monday. He urged Lagos residents, particularly those in the Lagos Central Senatorial District, to turn out in large numbers to vote for Tinubu and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The deputy governor said residents have a responsibility to support the President’s re-election, noting that Tinubu’s longstanding political connection to Lagos State made its support particularly significant. He added that re-electing the President would ensure continuity in the work his administration had begun. Hamzat noted that Lagos had the highest number of registered voters in the country, stressing the need to translate the figures into actual votes to achieve the desired electoral outcome. “We are commissioning this office today to take our campaign to the grassroots. We know Lagos Island has been doing really well in voting but that is not enough, as many people still do not vote. “We are here to mobilise residents to come out and vote for our President because he is one of us. “We must demonstrate our support by voting for his re-election so that he can continue the good works he has started,” he said. Hamzat also urged party members to encourage residents to participate in the elections, citing Osun, where he said about 54 per cent of registered voters participated in the last election, as an example of the need to improve voter turnout. The deputy governor urged the party members to mobilise others to vote, emphasising that political support must be demonstrated through participation at the polls. “My charge to you is that, as you are all seated here today, on election day, make sure you take someone along to the polling unit to vote for Tinubu. “It will be dangerous for us not to come out and vote for all our candidates if we truly say we love them,” Hamzat said. The Lagos State Chairman of the APC, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, said the campaign office would serve as a strategic platform for strengthening ties between the senatorial district and the state leadership. Ojelabi said the office would also facilitate the dissemination of the party’s policies and achievements across local governments, wards and polling units. He urged party members to serve as ambassadors by taking the messages on the achievements of Tinubu and Gov. Babajide Sanwo-Olu to the grassroots. Ojelabi also encouraged members who were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to do so promptly, while calling for peaceful campaigns, constructive, issue-based engagement and effective voter mobilisation ahead of the elections. Sen. Wasiu Eshilokun-Sanni, representing Lagos Central Senatorial District, described the inauguration of the campaign office as a historic milestone and a symbol of unity, peace and the party’s determination to consolidate its achievements. Eshilokun-Sanni urged party members and supporters to remain united in spite of their differences, engage constructively with their neighbours and maintain discipline throughout the electioneering process. He called for grassroots mobilisation and a stronger party presence across communities, markets and households. He expressed confidence that sustained engagement would help the APC achieve its electoral objectives in Lagos Central, Lagos State and Nigeria. Earlier, in his address, the Director-General of the PBAT/KOH Lagos Campaign Organisation, Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, described the inauguration of the Lagos central senatorial campaign office as a reaffirmation of the district’s political significance and strategic importance to the APC. Obanikoro said the facility underscored the party’s commitment to strengthening its political structures and consolidating its presence across the senatorial district. He urged party members and supporters to intensify campaign activities and grassroots mobilisation in support of Tinubu’s re-election and the electoral success of other APC candidates in the forthcoming elections. (NAN) The post Tinubu’s re-election crucial to Nigeria’s prosperity – Hamzat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NAPTIP ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‌‍⁠‍​‌​receives 105 Nigerians rescued from Ghana cybercrime syndicates
items.description: The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) says it has received 105 Nigerians rescued in a coordinated operation against cybercrime syndicates in Ghana. A statement issued on Monday by the agency’s Head of Press and Public Relations Unit, Mr Vincent Adekoye, says the rescue operation was in tandem with President Bola Tinubu’s citizen-focused policies. Adekoye said that the operation was coordinated by the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) after the Cyber Security Authority of Ghana contacted NAPTIP. He said that NAPTIP led the participating Nigerian Security and Law Enforcement agencies, including the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), the National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (NCFRMI). Others are the Department of State Services (DSS), the National Intelligence Agency (NIA), the Nigerian High Commission in Ghana, and the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria. He said that the development was hailed by a cross-section of stakeholders, including Civil Society Organisations and collaborating international organisations. Adekoye said the development underscored the commitment of the Federal Government of Nigeria to the safety of Nigerians, especially victims of human trafficking and irregular migration. He quoted the Ghanaian government as saying that 119 Nigerians were rescued during the operation, of which 105 were repatriated, while the remaining 14 are being processed. The statement also quoted the Director-General of NAPTIP, Hajia Binta Adamu-Bello, while receiving the survivors on-behalf of the Federal Government welcomed the returnees and assured them of their safety. She encouraged them to remain calm while the Federal Government carries out profiling and reintegration processes, adding that NAPTIP’s engagement with the returnees reflected the agency’s commitment to protecting their dignity. Adamu-Bello said that NAPTIP was committed to safeguarding their welfare and ensuring that each person received assistance suited to their individual circumstances. She expressed NAPTIP’s appreciation to the Ghanaian authorities, particularly the Cyber Security Authority of Ghana, Ghana Immigration Service, and the United Kingdom’s National Crime Agency (NCA) for its operational support. “The agency specially thanks the Office of the National Security Adviser, Nigerian security and law enforcement agencies, and all partners whose collaboration made the operation a huge success. “NAPTIP reaffirms its commitment to strengthening national and international cooperation against human trafficking and related forms of exploitation. “It will continue to ensure that individuals identified during such operations receive appropriate screening, protection and support according to their circumstances,” Adamu-Bello said. The NAPTIP boss urged Nigerians to exercise serious caution when considering employment, scholarships or other opportunities abroad. He specifically warned Nigerians to beware of offers that make unrealistic promises, give vague job descriptions, or involve suspicious recruitment arrangements. (NAN) The post NAPTIP ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‌‍⁠‍​‌​receives 105 Nigerians rescued from Ghana cybercrime syndicates appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Qantas flight grounded after bedbug outbreak
items.description: A Qantas flight from Italy to Australia was cancelled on Saturday, after an outbreak of bedbugs on the plane. During the previous flight on Friday – a nearly 17-hour journey from Perth to Rome – some passengers had complained that they were being bitten by bugs, according to the Sydney Morning Herald. They were reportedly given antihistamines to help ease the itch of the bites, but supplies ran out. The Boeing 787 Dreamliner had to be grounded for “a deep clean”, a Qantas spokesperson told the BBC. “We sincerely apologise to customers for the cancellation of Saturday’s Rome to Perth service, which allowed our engineers and maintenance teams to carry out a deep clean of the aircraft after an issue was identified on a small number of economy seats,” the spokesperson said. All affected customers were provided with accommodation and were rebooked on alternative flights within 48 hours of their original departure, the carrier said. Bedbugs are small, wingless parasites that can live on clothes, furniture and bedding. Their bites can be itchy but they do not usually cause more serious health problems, the NHS website says . But they can be difficult and expensive to get rid of. Treatment includes washing all bedding, clothing, and household materials like curtains on a hot wash and tumble dry, or they can be put in plastic bags in a freezer for three or four days. Bedbugs causing travel chaos is not unusual – less than two weeks ago, several Southeastern train services in England were cancelled after drivers discovered the creepy-crawlies in their cabs. In 2017, British Airways apologised to a family travelling from Vancouver to London, after they were left covered in bug bites from an overnight flight. And Turkish Airlines faced with a PR nightmare last year after the New York Times reported of several instances of bedbug infestations on its planes – and allegations at the time that the airline did nothing about it.

items.title: African Cybersecurity Forum 2026 : Maroc Telecom place la confiance numérique au cœur de sa stratégie
items.description: Présent à l’African Cybersecurity Forum 2026, organisé du 12 au 14 octobre à Rabat, Maroc Telecom met en avant son rôle dans la construction d’un environnement numérique plus sûr et résilient. À travers ses solutions de connectivité, de cybersécurité et de cloud souverain, mais aussi à travers les interventions de ses experts, le Groupe entend réaffirmer son engagement en faveur de la confiance numérique au Maroc et sur les marchés africains. Rabat accueille du 12 au 14 octobre l’African Cybersecurity Forum 2026, qui réunit au Four Seasons Kasr Al Bahr des acteurs publics et privés autour des grands enjeux de la cybersécurité en Afrique. Parmi les participants, Maroc Telecom occupe une place particulière en tant qu’opérateur d’infrastructures critiques et acteur de la transformation numérique. Le Groupe y présente une offre articulée autour de trois dimensions : connectivité critique, cybersécurité managée et cloud souverain hébergé au Maroc. Une approche qui s’inscrit dans un contexte où la multiplication des cybermenaces, le développement du cloud et l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle imposent aux organisations de renforcer simultanément leurs capacités de protection et leur résilience. Il n’y a pas de transformation sans confiance Pour Mohamed Laklalech, Chief Information & Technology Officer de Maroc Telecom, la cybersécurité constitue aujourd’hui un élément indissociable de la transformation numérique. « Il n’y a pas de transformation sans confiance. Et c’est aussi que la cybersécurité, elle est au service de cette transformation », souligne-t-il lors du Forum. Le responsable explique que Maroc Telecom agit sur deux fronts. Le premier consiste à assurer la protection des services et des données indispensables aux activités de ses clients, à travers la sécurisation de ses infrastructures, de ses data centers, de ses réseaux et de son cloud. Cette protection vise notamment à garantir la continuité des services et à renforcer la sécurité des entreprises et des institutions qui s’appuient sur ces infrastructures. Le deuxième axe concerne l’accompagnement des clients dans leurs propres projets de transformation numérique. Maroc Telecom combine ainsi, selon Mohamed Laklalech, des offres de connectivité avec des services d’hébergement, de souveraineté, de cloud et de cybersécurité. « Tout cela dans une ambition très claire qui est de contribuer à un Maroc numérique sûr, résilient », résume-t-il. © Souhail Rmidi Le cloud souverain comme couche supplémentaire de sécurité La question de la souveraineté des données occupe également une place centrale dans la présence du Groupe au Forum. Mehdi Benamar, Chief Information Security Officer – Cybersecurity chez Maroc Telecom, souligne l’importance croissante du cloud dans le développement numérique du pays, tout en mettant en avant la nécessité d’accompagner cette évolution par des dispositifs de sécurité adaptés. Maroc Telecom a ainsi mis en place un cloud souverain permettant à ses clients de conserver leurs données au Maroc, dans ses propres data centers. Selon Mehdi Benamar, cette localisation constitue une couche de sécurité supplémentaire pour les données les plus sensibles. L’enjeu est également de garantir plusieurs dimensions essentielles pour les entreprises et institutions : la confidentialité des données, la maîtrise des accès et la continuité d’activité en cas d’incident ou de cyberattaque. « La souveraineté numérique et la cybersécurité sont deux piliers pour un Maroc digital de confiance », affirme-t-il. Cette vision se retrouve également sur le stand de Maroc Telecom, conçu autour de plusieurs espaces consacrés à la confiance numérique. L’espace Protected Data présente notamment les solutions de cybersécurité managée du Groupe, avec le SD-WAN et les services MSSP permettant de sécuriser les différents sites d’une entreprise, ainsi que la protection DDoS destinée à contribuer à la continuité des services. Avec Critical Connectivity, Maroc Telecom met en avant sa solution de Wi-Fi managé, offrant une connectivité sécurisée aux collaborateurs, visiteurs et objets connectés, avec une gestion centralisée des différents sites. Le volet Sovereign Cloud présente pour sa part l’offre permettant aux entreprises et institutions d’héberger leurs ressources cloud au Maroc, dans un data center certifié Tier III et destiné notamment aux applications critiques. Le Groupe expose également les possibilités offertes par la 5G Industrial Intelligence, qui associe la connectivité 5G de Maroc Telecom à l’intelligence artificielle pour illustrer différents usages industriels. Du cloud à la cybersécurité quantique La participation de Maroc Telecom s’étend également aux différents panels du Forum. Les responsables du Groupe interviennent notamment sur les stratégies nationales de cybersécurité, la transformation numérique sécurisée par le cloud, les partenariats public-privé et le développement du marché de la cybersécurité comme moteur de croissance et d’innovation. Un autre temps fort porte sur un sujet encore émergent mais appelé à transformer profondément les stratégies de sécurité : la cybersécurité à l’ère quantique. © Souhail Rmidi Les experts de Maroc Telecom animent ainsi le workshop « Naviguer l’horizon quantique : construire des cyberdéfenses nationales résilientes avec les réseaux quantiques sécurisés ». Les échanges portent notamment sur les risques que les futurs ordinateurs quantiques pourraient faire peser sur certains mécanismes de chiffrement actuels, mais aussi sur les enjeux de gouvernance, de coopération internationale et de normalisation. Construire un Maroc numérique de confiance À travers cette participation, Maroc Telecom entend ainsi inscrire la cybersécurité dans une vision plus large de la transformation numérique : celle d’un écosystème où la connectivité, le cloud, la protection des données et la résilience doivent évoluer conjointement. Pour Mohamed Laklalech comme pour Mehdi Benamar, le même principe se dégage : la transformation numérique ne peut durablement s’appuyer que sur la confiance. Une approche que le Groupe met en avant à Rabat, à la fois à travers ses infrastructures, ses solutions de cybersécurité et de cloud souverain, mais aussi à travers le partage d’expertise avec les acteurs publics et privés réunis à l’African Cybersecurity Forum 2026. The post African Cybersecurity Forum 2026 : Maroc Telecom place la confiance numérique au cœur de sa stratégie appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Obasanjo urges increase in 13% derivation for oil-producing states
items.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo on Monday advocated an increase in the 13 per cent derivation allocated to oil-producing states. Obasanjo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‍​⁠‌⁠‌​spoke at the inauguration of the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU) of Azikel Refinery at Obunagha, Yenagoa Local Government Area of Bayelsa. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the one-billion-dollar refinery project is owned by Azikel Petroleum, under the Azikel Group. The refinery is expected to produce 2.5 million litres of petrol and two million litres of diesel daily, alongside other petroleum products. Obasanjo commended Azikel Group President, Dr Azibapu Eruani, for initiating the project and urged him to ensure its completion within 12 months. He also appreciated the refinery’s technical and engineering team, African Finance Corporation (AFC) and Afreximbank for supporting the project. The former president called for continued support to facilitate the refinery’s completion, noting that its development had progressed significantly since his previous visit. Obasanjo also commended Gov. Douye Diri of Bayelsa for supporting the project and effectively utilising the state’s revenue, citing numerous development projects. “I have told Dr Eruani that I will be officially 90 years by next March. It means I will take the boarding pass soon. “He has to make sure the project is completed before I exit,” he said. Addressing Diri, Obasanjo said Eruani had consistently acknowledged the governor’s critical contribution to the refinery project. “You are right that the states and oil-producing communities have not got a fair deal so far. Thirteen per cent is the beginning. “You can continue to talk. The most important thing is that even the little you have received, you have used it well,” he said. Obasanjo challenged Eruani to complete the refinery within the next 12 months, adding that its capacity could subsequently be doubled. Speaking earlier, Eruani said the refinery would kick-start industrialisation in Bayelsa and the wider Niger Delta region. He recalled that Obasanjo laid the refinery’s foundation eight years ago, describing the installation of the CDU as a major step toward completing the project. Eruani said the refinery was conceived to make the Niger Delta an active participant in the petroleum industry. He described it as the country’s second-largest full-scale refinery and commended President Bola Tinubu for supporting indigenous refineries. According to him, local refining aligns with the Federal Government’s vision of making petroleum products available and affordable. Eruani also appreciated Diri, AFC and Afreximbank for their contributions to the project. In his remarks, Diri said the refinery vindicated years of agitation by Niger Delta communities against perceived injustice in the petroleum industry. He argued that communities producing crude oil deserved to become key participants in the industry and benefit more substantially from their natural resources. The governor criticised the Land Use Act and the existing 13 per cent derivation formula, insisting that oil-producing states deserved a greater share of their resources. “The Land Use Act is unfair. Surface resources belong to states, but what lies underneath belongs to the Federal Government. “That law is obnoxious and not good for any just society,” he said. Diri said the region was not seeking to take everything for itself but wanted to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning its resources. “We do not want to take all to ourselves. We just want to be co-players in determining how it is done. Thirteen per cent is not enough for the states,” he said. The governor expressed delight that the refinery would position Bayelsans to participate more actively in the petroleum industry. He urged residents to equip themselves with the necessary skills to benefit from the opportunities the project would create. Diri also stressed that Africa must process its own natural resources to maximise their economic benefits. He called on oil companies operating in the Gbarain/Obunagha area to complement the state government’s efforts by rehabilitating the road leading to the refinery. (NAN) The post Obasanjo urges increase in 13% derivation for oil-producing states appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Reality Zone with Vicky Wireko: International Day of the Girl, shaping today’s girl for tomorrow’s future – ZONTA Clubs lead the way
items.description: Sunday, October 11, is a day set aside by the United Nations for worldwide recognition of girls’ rights as it celebrates International Day of the Girl. And why the girl? The 2030 Agenda for the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) guides world leaders and global communities to work together to realise the human rights of all people, eradicate poverty and protect the planet for future generations. Reportedly, nine out of these 17 goals are explicit about women, with SDG 5 dedicated to gender equality and women’s empowerment. It states in part as follows: “Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls”. It goes without saying, therefore, that in order to achieve SDG 5, the world should be intentional about its direction and pace up with programmes and activities that would help in the achievement of the global deadline by 2030. Development of women and girls Consequently, some committed organisations, global and local and conscious of making impact are working actively towards achievement of some of the goals, if not all. Issues impinging on the development of women and girls in societies, for example, and which border on poverty, equality, education, health as well as climate change are highlighted. They are issues that cut across many countries in the world, and no wonder they feature in the 17 SDGs. Subsequently, those global and local organisations who are working with or championing the cause of women and girls have committed to making a difference as well as supporting what national governments have decided to do. One such global organisation is Zonta International. Zonta international Zonta International is a not-for-profit organisation that works across 65 countries in the world to progress the human rights of women and girls while unlocking the opportunities that exist for them in their societies. For this and many reasons, Zonta International, on the occasion of the International recognition of girls, has singled out one of the tenets of SDG 5, which states: “Eliminate all harmful practices, such as child, early and forced marriage.” In celebrating the International Day of the Girl this year, therefore, the organisation has selected as its theme a call to end child marriage now. It is one of the biggest battles to overcome in those countries that are perpetuating child brides as far as violence against girls is concerned. Statistics In the Ghanaian context, available statistics confirm a progression toward reducing the problem of early marriage. Per UNFPA and UNICEF statistics, in 2021, there were 2.2 million child brides in the country. Out of that number, 662,200 were married before the age of 15. The current prevalence of girls marrying before the age of 18 is 19 percent. This is said to be one of the lowest in West and Central Africa, which has a Regional average of 37 per cent. Though the statistics might be encouraging, unfortunately, they are not encouraging enough to meet the goal to end child marriage by 2030 as stipulated in SDG 5.3, which states: ‘Eliminate all harmful practices such as child, early and forced marriage and female genital mutilation.” Early marriages cause more harm than good to the girls and society. The practice, born out of poverty and sometimes ignorance, truncates girls’ education mid-stream. It blocks the chances of better economic empowerment in the future, apart from being a human rights issue. Zonta Clubs Zonta Clubs in Ghana affirm the clarion call by its mother organisation, Zonta International by advocating strongly against underage marriage for girls stressing the denial such practices lead to- denial of the children’s rights to education, health, safety and equal opportunities. It is time for our lawmakers to spruce up the existing laws on child rights while introducing more child marriage laws and policies, for example. It is time for the government to introduce more incentives that would help girls progress through their education to higher heights. These are some of the measures that would help the nation achieve its SDG 5. In Ghana, Zonta International has its presence in five very active clubs, namely: Zonta Club of Accra, Zonta Club of Tema, Zonta Club of Accra II, Zonta Club of Accra Metropolitan and Zonta Club of Accra Jubilee. These clubs are all working assiduously to build a better world, particularly for Ghanaian women and girls. As the world celebrates girls on 11 th October 2026 as World Girls’ Day, the Zonta Clubs wish to remind us all and the world at large about our collective role to help end child marriage now. Through the work they have done through activities and advocacy so far, they are asking for partnerships in government, organisations and individuals committed to girls’ development to join forces and hold hands together to sing ”Hail to our Zonta Club, trustworthy true…” They pledge their loyal hearts and strength to commit their budgets and time to work on matters that will open doors for a better world for women and girls. On the occasion of the 2026 International Day of the Girl, Zonta Ghana’s call is to say no to child brides as the country marches on to claim the prize of achieving SDG5 in 2030. Writer’s email: vickywirekoandoh@yahoo.com

items.title: Guinée : les dates des élections sénatoriales et régionales fixées (décret)
items.description: Le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya a fixé les dates des élections des conseillers régionaux et des sénateurs en Guinée. Selon un décret lu à la télévision nationale ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, les deux scrutins se tiendront respectivement les 29 novembre et 20 décembre prochains. Les électeurs guinéens sont ainsi fixés sur le calendrier de ces deux échéances électorales, qui concerneront l’ensemble du territoire national ainsi que la zone spéciale de Conakry. Selon le calendrier annoncé, l’élection des conseillers régionaux est prévue le dimanche 29 novembre 2026, sur toute l’étendue du territoire national, y compris dans la zone spéciale de Conakry. L’élection des deux tiers des membres du Sénat, quant à elle, se tiendra le dimanche 20 décembre 2026.

items.title: You’ve nothing to fear in Tinubu’s 2nd term – Shettima tells North
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru Vice President Kashim Shettima has issued a rallying cry to the North for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 presidential election, declaring that the region has absolutely nothing to fear from a second term for the President. With urgent intensity, he implored northern leaders and citizens to unite behind the President’s re-election bid, framing the administration’s second-term agenda as a secure, bulletproof guarantee for the region’s future prosperity and stability. Senator Shettima made the call on Monday when he received, on a courtesy visit, a delegation from the Arewa for Tinubu (A4A) – a northern-based think tank -:working for the re-election of President Tinubu. He called on leaders across the region to unite into a single front and work for the progress of the area and the well-being of its people, which are top priorities for the Tinubu administration. According to the VP, the North has no reason to be scared of the re-election of President Tinubu, as it has benefitted immensely in terms of appointments and game-changing projects and programmes. His words: “Let’s unite as a people and work for the development of our region and the progress of our people through the re-election of this administration. We are benefiting and we stand to benefit more from this government in many ways. “The Bank of Agriculture has disbursed N450 billion to 700,000 smallholder farmers in Nigeria and about 70 percent of the beneficiaries are from the north. “The present administration is working towards completing landmark and groundbreaking projects in parts of the country. I can assure you that the president loves the north and the president will work for the north.” The Vice President thanked the group for their steadfast support for President Tinubu at all times and appealed to them to work harder and galvanise across wards, communities and local governments in the northern region for the President’s re-election. Earlier, the Director General of the Area for Asiwaju and former Jigawa State Governor, Abubakar Badaru, said the organisation will not rest on its laurels until they make the North proud by reelecting Tinubu. He said the group plans to meet with religious leaders, including Muslim and Christian clerics, as well as other prominent Nigerians to explain to them the need to support the Tinubu/Shettima ticket in 2027. “On discussions with the high-profile, we have gone far. We have met them severally and the BoT is meeting them again to consolidate our gains and to tell them why there is need to support this ticket. “We are also supporting the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) with whatever they want us to do that is micro in nature because they are so big and we really don’t want to lose sight of the bigger arrangement that is there. We want to focus very well on the contacts at the grassroots – the local government areas and the wards.” Also, Chairman of the organisation’s Board of Trustees (BoT) and former Kano State Governor, Ibrahim Shekarau, said the think tank which worked for President Tinubu’s election in the 2023 general election will repeat the same feat in 2027. He said the organisation had been meeting with northern governors and other stakeholders to compare notes and collaborate on areas of working together to achieve the President’s reelection. He noted that the organisation has concluded plans to have a full-fledged secretariat for purposes of coordination, where there will be offices for directors and state coordinators to compare reports, analyse them, and give out instructions to its members. The BoT Chairman formally invited the Vice President to officially commission the A4A office complex on Saturday, October 17, 2027. Also present at the meeting were former governors of Plateau, Joshua Dariye and Senator Simon Lalong; Taraba, Rev. Jolly Nyame; Kogi, Yahaya Bello; Katsina, Ibrahim Shehu Shema; Bauchi, Isa Yuguda; Special Adviser to the President on Policy and Coordination, Hadiza Bala Usman; Chairman of NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd), some top officials of government, and other members of the A4A BOT and Secretariat. The post You’ve nothing to fear in Tinubu’s 2nd term – Shettima tells North appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Trump’s October Surprise
items.description: I t rained most of Sunday in Washington, as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias washed over the East Coast. Unable to golf, and stuck inside the White House, President Trump spent part of his morning on social media touting the size of his rallies and defending Christopher Columbus. He also declared that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt strikes against each other’s energy infrastructures. Except that he hadn’t first confirmed that with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky—and Russia spent the hours that followed bombarding Ukraine with missiles and drones, hitting a Kharkiv power plant. Trump’s inability to bring the Iran war to a close has left him incensed but also oddly paralyzed, two people close to him told us. One of them, an adviser, said that Trump “is used to snapping his fingers and having the whole world—Republicans, world leaders, the media—come to attention, and he is losing his mind that Iran won’t listen.” Iran has resumed menacing oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and the average price of diesel in the United States has crossed the $6-a-gallon mark, raising the cost of goods that travel the nation’s highways on trucks. Republicans are panicked that those high energy prices could help Democrats take control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, which are now only three weeks away. Trump has been searching for a scapegoat, and appears to have settled on Ukraine. Although blaming a European country that’s fighting for its existence for the rise in global oil prices might seem implausible, Trump seems to prefer that to accepting responsibility for his decision to attack Iran. His broadsides against Ukraine, moreover, are consistent with his decade-long deference to Vladimir Putin. With rare exceptions, Trump has aligned with Moscow over Kyiv throughout the four-and-a-half-year war. He wants Ukraine to end the fighting—and has pressured the country to agree to terms that Zelensky finds unacceptable. A U.S. president siding with the Kremlin is quite an October surprise . But in just the past few days, Trump appears to have fully turned against Ukraine. He announced on Friday that he had reached an agreement with Putin to import Russian diesel fuel, undercutting the new sanctions bill against Moscow’s energy industry that Trump signed into law last month. Even if the roughly 2.25 million barrels headed to the U.S. only marginally ease fuel costs, the deal allows Trump to tout efforts to help Americans while also providing Russia with additional revenue. (Another few million barrels are set to ship next month.) Despite the opposition of European allies and some Republicans on Capitol Hill, Trump has followed up by placing even more pressure on Ukraine. He called for Zelensky to be replaced. His aides have threatened to withhold arms sales unless Kyiv stops targeting Russian diesel plants. Some in Trump’s orbit have suggested that the U.S. go further, and stop sharing intelligence with Kyiv. That was the context in which Trump announced his fictional energy cease-fire. A senior Ukrainian military officer told us that Trump’s statements are “simply beyond comprehension.” “Things are already incredibly difficult for us here,” the officer said, speaking, like others who talked with us, on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters. “But apparently, there’s always another level below rock bottom. Things can always get worse.” U kraine has expanded its strikes deep into Russian territory in recent months, targeting the larger nation’s oil refineries. Those attacks sparked an energy crisis in Russia and were cheered across Europe—but not in the White House. Russia imposed a ban on diesel exports in response, which added more pressure to global diesel markets already under strain from the war in Iran. Zelensky told Trump and his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner that he was willing to stop attacking Russian oil refineries if the Russians halted attacks on Ukrainian power plants, a White House official told us. But Trump doesn’t see the strikes as equivalent—and demanded that Ukraine first stop attacking Russian refineries, the official said. Zelensky refused. “Zelensky is overplaying his hand and pissing the president off,” the White House official said. “The president is asking for one thing: stop hitting the refineries. Give him that.” [ Read: Trump’s latest appeal to Russia could outrage even his allies ] Trump’s next move against Ukraine came, as it so often does, after a phone call with Putin. Zelensky’s aides have expressed frustration that Putin has swayed Trump at crucial junctures in the conflict (once, even, while Zelensky was flying to Washington to meet with Trump in an effort to secure access to new U.S. weapons). This time, Trump spoke with Putin on Friday to wish him a belated birthday, even though some in the White House counseled against the call, the adviser told us, believing it would yield little. During the 90-minute conversation, Trump told Putin that he would lift the sanctions on Russian diesel exports. (Some in Kyiv believe that the deal was agreed to earlier, because a ship carrying Russian oil and gas is already approaching the U.S.) That undermined sanctions applied in 2022 and undercut the tougher Russian-sanctions bill that Trump signed last month; the law was named in honor of one of its champions, the late Senator Lindsey Graham. A bipartisan group of lawmakers was infuriated by the move, and some Republicans denounced Trump for siding with Putin. Four GOP senators—Lisa Murkowski of Alaska, Susan Collins of ⁠Maine, Thom Tillis of North Carolina, and John Curtis of Utah—joined some of their Democratic colleagues to release a statement yesterday saying that lifting the sanctions “runs directly counter to that law” and that the U.S. should not provide “Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians.” Zelensky, who was blindsided by the diesel deal, deemed it “not fair and not honest.” He had spent more than a year trying to repair his relationship with Trump, which hit its nadir in February 2025 during a shouting match in the Oval Office. Since then, Zelensky has taken to flattering the U.S. president, and he has tried to capitalize on Trump’s occasional annoyance that Putin will not end the war. Trump and Putin’s Alaska summit last year yielded little more than a photo of the two that hangs in the Palm Room at the White House. Even if Trump wouldn’t fully support Ukraine, officials in Kyiv had hoped he would not actively hurt their cause. That hope may be fading. Recent talks between Kushner, Witkoff, and Putin have included the promise of massive business deals that Russia could strike with U.S. interests once the war concludes, according to reports . Ukrainian officials have long believed that Trump’s foreign policy focuses on opening up business deals—and the potential enrichment of the president’s family and friends—over the defense of democracy, human rights, or territorial sovereignty. Some officials in Kyiv believe that Russia’s economy, which has been remade to fuel Putin’s war machine, will not implode, despite the pressure of increased drone strikes and sanctions. A Ukrainian official close to the negotiating process told us that means “we need to change our strategy, stop fooling ourselves,” and find a way out of the war with Europe’s help. That, the official said, would likely require a new emphasis on negotiations. During his call with Trump, Putin declined to commit to resuming peace talks, the Kremlin later told reporters. Yet Trump continues to view Zelensky as the primary impediment to peace—and the business deals it might bring—and he called for Ukraine to hold elections to select a new president. (Zelensky has said he will hold an election if Putin agrees to a 60-day cease-fire.) Trump also views Zelensky as an obstacle to his coveted, yet elusive, Nobel Peace Prize, for which he was passed over again last week. A senior European official told us that the U.S. has threatened to stop selling weapons to Ukraine via Europe if the strikes continue, and some close to Trump have suggested that the U.S. stop sharing intelligence with Ukraine, as it briefly did after the 2025 Oval Office argument. [ From the November 2026 issue: The Baltic states prepare for war ] Ukraine was already bracing for a difficult winter. Moscow has escalated its attacks on Ukraine’s cities. It has grown its missile stockpiles and debuted a jet-powered drone that Ukrainian defenses have had difficulty stopping. Europe has tried to fill the gaps left by Trump’s indifference—and the U.S. being bogged down in Iran—but Zelensky’s aides believe that Putin will use the winter to pummel their cities before making another lunge at Kyiv in the spring. If, suddenly, Ukraine were left without U.S. intelligence or American-made weapons, Kyiv might be in its most vulnerable position since the first days of the war. T rump’s admiration for Putin has been one of the most enduring geopolitical subplots of the past decade. He refused to publicly acknowledge Russia’s efforts to help elect him in 2016, infamously siding with Putin over U.S. intelligence agencies during the leaders’ summit in Helsinki during his first term. More recently, he has refrained from holding Putin to account for helping Iran, even after American intelligence agencies revealed that Moscow gave Tehran targeting information to strike U.S. military assets in the region. Some of Trump’s closest outside advisers have privately wondered what Putin has done to so thoroughly enthrall the president; Trump’s respect for the Russian leader appears undiminished despite the humiliating struggles Putin has faced during the Ukraine invasion. Instead, Trump has taken steps to help Putin shed his status as an international pariah. Though Putin has been charged with war crimes by the International Criminal Court, Trump welcomed him to Anchorage last summer. Trump’s move to undo the diesel sanctions could provide a boost to Russia’s faltering economy. And he has overruled the objections of some in his own party by inviting Putin to this winter’s G20 summit, which the United States is hosting at a Trump-owned golf course in Doral, just outside Miami. If Putin accepts the invitation to that December meeting, it would be the first time he has attended a multilateral summit in a Western country since his invasion of Ukraine. Zelensky has said he’ll be there, and is hoping to meet with Putin to negotiate the end of the war. Trump has mentioned to advisers, one of them told us, that he’d like both sides to arrive to Doral ready to make a deal, so he can then preside over a peacemaking summit. Maybe then, Trump has suggested, he can finally win that Nobel.

items.title: Dr Mame Aminata Ndir, dermatologue: « Les produits dépigmentants peuvent entraîner plusieurs complications »
items.description: Alors que les réseaux sociaux contribuent à banaliser la quête du teint clair, les produits dépigmentants suscitent des inquiétudes croissantes dans le milieu médical. Troubles pigmentaires, infections cutanées, diabète, hypertension artérielle, difficultés de cicatrisation et risque de cancer de la peau figurent parmi les complications évoquées par Dr Mame Aminata Ndir, dermatologue. Dans cet entretien, elle alerte sur les dangers de l’utilisation prolongée de l’hydroquinone et des corticoïdes, et appelle à une meilleure prise de conscience des conséquences de la dépigmentation sur la santé. Entretien Quels sont les risques liés à l’utilisation des produits éclaircissants, notamment l’hydroquinone et les corticoïdes ? Les produits dépigmentants peuvent entraîner plusieurs complications. Concernant l’hydroquinone, les effets les plus fréquemment observés sont les troubles pigmentaires, notamment l’ochronose exogène, qui se manifeste par une coloration anormale de la peau. Certaines lésions peuvent devenir particulièrement préoccupantes avec l’exposition au soleil. Concernant le risque de cancer de la peau, il existe de nombreuses inquiétudes médicales. Les corticoïdes, souvent présents dans les mélanges éclaircissants, peuvent provoquer de nombreuses complications cutanées. Ils fragilisent la peau et favorisent les infections bactériennes, les abcès, la gale et les infections fongiques. Dans certains cas, les complications peuvent nécessiter une hospitalisation, notamment en cas d’érysipèle, une infection cutanée qui touche fréquemment les membres inférieurs. On peut également observer des vergetures et un amincissement de la peau. Lorsque les corticoïdes sont absorbés par l’organisme, leur utilisation excessive ou prolongée peut entraîner des complications générales, notamment une élévation de la glycémie, un diabète, une hypertension artérielle et, dans certaines circonstances, une atteinte rénale. Comment la dépigmentation fragilise-t-elle la peau et quels signes doivent alerter les utilisateurs ? La mélanine joue un rôle essentiel dans la protection de la peau contre les rayons ultraviolets. Certains produits dépigmentants perturbent sa production ou sa répartition. En réduisant cette protection naturelle, ils peuvent rendre la peau plus vulnérable aux effets du soleil et à certaines lésions cutanées. Le niveau de risque dépend toutefois des substances utilisées et de leur mode d’utilisation. Plusieurs signes doivent alerter les personnes qui utilisent ces produits. Une prise de poids inhabituelle peut notamment être liée à l’utilisation prolongée de corticoïdes puissants, qui peuvent aussi perturber le métabolisme du sucre et modifier la répartition des graisses. Il faut également surveiller l’apparition de plaies, de vergetures, d’un amincissement de la peau ou de lésions pigmentaires persistantes sur le visage et le dos. Une accumulation anormale de graisse à la base du cou, appelée bosse de bison, peut évoquer un excès d’exposition aux corticoïdes. Face à ces signes, une consultation médicale s’impose. Quels sont les dangers de ces produits et quelles complications avez-vous rencontrées dans votre pratique ? L’utilisation de corticoïdes puissants, notamment dans des préparations dépigmentantes appliquées sur de grandes surfaces corporelles pendant une période prolongée, peut présenter des risques pour la mère et le fœtus. Certains effets indésirables peuvent toucher le développement du bébé. Les risques dépendent toutefois du produit utilisé, de la dose et de la durée d’exposition. La dépigmentation peut également compliquer la prise en charge chirurgicale. Une peau fragilisée peut présenter des difficultés de cicatrisation. Dans le cas d’une césarienne, cela peut notamment compromettre la bonne cicatrisation de la plaie opératoire et compliquer les soins postopératoires. Dans ma pratique, j’ai rencontré des cas de cancer, de nombreux cas de diabète et d’hypertension artérielle, ainsi que des complications cutanées. Par Amadou KÉBÉ

items.title: Prix UNESCO 2026 : Peng Liyuan félicite le Maroc pour son engagement en faveur de l’éducation des adolescentes
items.description: La cérémonie de remise du Prix UNESCO 2026 pour l’éducation des filles et des femmes s’est tenue le vendredi 9 octobre 2026 à Paris. Peng Liyuan, épouse du Président Chinois Xi Jinping et envoyée spéciale de l’UNESCO pour la promotion de l’éducation des filles et des femmes, a adressé une allocution vidéo à la cérémonie. Mme Peng a adressé de chaleureuses félicitations aux lauréats de cette année, du Maroc et du Pérou. Soulignant que l’éducation des filles et des femmes est un indicateur clé du progrès de la civilisation humaine, elle a déclaré qu’au cours des dernières années, grâce au fort plaidoyer de l’UNESCO et aux efforts concertés de la communauté internationale, des progrès encourageants avaient été réalisés dans cette noble cause. Insistant sur le fait que la Chine a toujours accordé une grande importance à l’éducation des filles et des femmes, Mme Peng a affirmé que la Chine menait de manière active et approfondie une coopération concrète avec l’UNESCO et les parties concernées, au bénéfice des femmes de nombreux pays. Elle a indiqué que les efforts déployés par la Chine ces dernières années pour recourir à l’IA afin de favoriser une éducation de qualité avaient non seulement renforcé l’égalité des sexes dans l’éducation et l’épanouissement global des femmes, mais aussi offert une expérience utile aux pays du Sud global. Soulignant que l’éducation des filles et des femmes demeure une tâche ardue, elle a exhorté la communauté internationale à unir ses efforts pour renforcer l’enseignement et la formation professionnels des femmes, développer vigoureusement l’éducation numérique et intelligente des femmes, afin qu’elles puissent utiliser les technologies numériques et intelligentes et en bénéficier pleinement, et leur construire une échelle vers une vie brillante. En faisant progresser l’éducation des filles et des femmes, on sème l’espoir, on nourrit les rêves et on récoltera le bonheur en abondance, a-t-elle dit. « Je suis prête à travailler avec vous tous pour promouvoir de plus grands progrès dans l’éducation des filles et des femmes et contribuer à un avenir plus radieux, où davantage de femmes pourront s’épanouir et briller » , a ajouté Mme Peng. Depuis que la Chine a créé ce prix en coopération avec l’UNESCO en 2015, celui-ci continue d’exercer un impact positif et a suscité une large attention ainsi qu’une haute reconnaissance de la part de la communauté internationale. Lors de cette cérémonie, le projet marocain, « Project Soar » a été récompensé pour son initiative « Project Soar dans une Valise ». Ce projet aide des adolescentes en situation défavorisée, au Maroc et dans d’autres régions, à poursuivre leur scolarité et à planifier leur avenir. Depuis 2017, ce projet a bénéficié à plus de 8000 adolescentes dans cinq pays. The post Prix UNESCO 2026 : Peng Liyuan félicite le Maroc pour son engagement en faveur de l’éducation des adolescentes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JCC 2026 | Une affiche célébrant 60 ans de passion cinématographique
items.description: L’identité visuelle de la 37ᵉ édition des JCC célèbre soixante ans de passion et d’engagement en faveur d’un cinéma africain et arabe qui défend les voix libres, les causes justes et des esthétiques visuelles singulières et novatrices. Au cœur du visage, le chiffre « 60 », subtilement dessiné par les lignes géométriques et la pellicule, rend hommage à six décennies de cinéma, de culture et de résistance par l’image. Le portrait stylisé, inspiré du cubisme et du Bauhaus, décline le visage en formes géométriques exprimant la diversité des genres cinématographiques et la pluralité des regards. La pellicule qui traverse la composition et épouse les contours du visage, symbolise la capacité du cinéma à raconter l’humain et la société. Le fond sombre et les textures granuleuses rappellent l’atmosphère de la salle de cinéma avant la projection, tandis que le contraste entre ombre et lumière en évoque la magie. L’orange et le rouge expriment la chaleur méditerranéenne et la passion du public, tandis que le bleu turquoise apporte sérénité et modernité. L’affiche allie audace esthétique et profondeur symbolique, rendant hommage aux fondateurs et à l’héritage des JCC, tout en affirmant le festival comme un espace de mémoire, de création et de rencontre. items.title: Lekki property: How Blessing CEO deceived me, collected my N69m — Witness tells court
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Social media influencer Blessing Nkiruka, popularly known as Blessing CEO, allegedly deceived a businessman into paying N69.15 million for a five-year lease of a Lekki property she did not own, a prosecution witness has told a Lagos court. Dr Onuoha Okeigwe said he paid the money after the influencer allegedly presented the property at No. 1 Tunbosun Osobu Street, Lekki, as hers. But the deal took a troubling turn when a man identified as Mr Tom reportedly showed up with police officers and arrested some of the workers at the premises. “I informed the defendant, and she claimed she did not know Mr Tom. I paid N100,000 to secure the release of my workers. Blessing still maintained that she did not know Mr Tom and that she was the owner of the property,” Okeigwe told the court. The witness, who testified as the first prosecution witness, said he had WhatsApp messages in which Blessing CEO allegedly sent him photographs of the building as evidence of her ownership. He also said he paid additional agency, legal and caution fees in connection with the transaction. Okeigwe further alleged that the influencer collected money from another person for the same property, insisting that the central issue was her alleged claim to ownership when she was not the actual owner. The allegations form the basis of a two-count charge filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Lagos Zonal Directorate 1, accusing Blessing CEO of obtaining money by false pretence and stealing N69.15 million. The EFCC alleged that on or about March 21, 2025, she induced Hope Chiropractic Health Clinic Limited to part with the money by falsely representing that she owned the Lekki property and was leasing it to the company for five years. Blessing CEO was arraigned on June 9, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the charges. Justice R. A. Oshodi of the Special Offences Court, Ikeja, adjourned the case until October 26, 2026, for continuation of the trial. items.title: Du débat d’idées à l’attaque personnelle : Amar Belani recadre le360.ma
items.description: Voici une réaction courte et sobre à une vieille connaissance, le site marocain le360.ma , qui me suit avec une assiduité remarquable depuis une quinzaine d’années. Il n'en mérite pas davantage. Le360.ma , considéré comme proche des cercles du pouvoir marocain, préfère manifestement la mise en cause de l’auteur à la réfutation de ses arguments. Cette dérive vers l’attaque ad hominem mérite quelques observations. Obsession Le décompte minutieux de mes articles, l’examen de mon parcours et le suivi constant de mes prises de parole relèvent davantage de l’obsession que de l’analyse critique. Visiblement, mes écrits lui donnent de l'urticaire plutôt que de la matière. Lorsque la personne devient le sujet principal et que les idées passent au second plan, le journalisme s’éloigne du débat pour glisser vers le règlement de comptes. Un procédé déshonorant, s’il en est. Après quinze ans d’attention soutenue, le360.ma devrait pourtant savoir qu’une attaque personnelle ne réfute jamais un argument. items.title: Global health must be led by countries, not designed for them – Mintah Akandoh
items.description: Ghana has renewed its call for a country-led global health system, with Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh telling the World Health Summit in Berlin that international health policies must be shaped with countries rather than imposed on them. His remarks come after the government rejected a proposed US$109 million health compact with the United States, citing concerns about provisions involving Ghana’s health data, financing obligations and regulatory authority. Addressing the summit in Germany, Mr Akandoh said countries must have a central role in determining the future of global health. “The answer from Ghana is a clear one. Global health must not be designed for countries; it must be designed with countries and led by countries,” he said. The position reflects the government’s emphasis on health sovereignty, including protecting national decision-making authority and strengthening domestic capacity to finance and manage healthcare. Ghana rejected the proposed five-year US health compact in April 2026 after reviewing its terms. President John Dramani Mahama subsequently explained that the agreement raised concerns over requirements relating to Ghana’s pathogen profile and citizens’ medical records. He also cited proposed counterpart funding obligations and provisions he said would restrict the Food and Drugs Authority’s ability to inspect medicines and other medical products supplied under the programme. The proposed agreement was intended to provide about US$109 million in American health assistance over five years, as Washington sought to restructure aspects of its foreign health support and require recipient countries to assume greater responsibility for financing their health programmes. The government’s rejection brought into focus the tension between securing external health financing and protecting national control over sensitive data, health regulation and policy decisions. The issue remains open to further discussion. On October 10, President Mahama disclosed that the United States had approached Ghana to review the rejected compact, with the government prepared to engage on provisions it considers unacceptable. At the Berlin summit, Mr Akandoh said Ghana’s position was consistent with President Mahama’s earlier address in Accra, which he described as a call to move “from dependency to dignity, from fragmentation to solidarity, from the promises of partnership to shared leadership”. He cited the government’s free primary healthcare initiative, the Mahama Cares programme, increased investment in immunisation and domestic resource mobilisation as measures intended to translate that vision into action. The minister did not provide specific funding figures or implementation details for the initiatives in his address. Mr Akandoh argued that countries must develop the capacity to withstand health emergencies rather than rely primarily on external assistance. “Resilience is not imported, and it is not donated. It must be built at home,” he said. The position comes amid wider concerns about African countries’ reliance on external sources for vaccines, medicines, health financing and other critical supplies. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed weaknesses in global access to medical products and differences in countries’ ability to secure supplies during emergencies. For Ghana, the debate extends beyond the terms of one bilateral agreement to questions about sustainable health financing, domestic production capacity and the protection of national health information. Mr Akandoh urged governments and other stakeholders to work together to improve health outcomes while allowing countries a greater role in setting priorities. “At this point, I want to call up all of you from Accra to Jakarta to Berlin; let us all come together to reset to save more lives,” he said. The World Health Summit brings together representatives from government, science, the private sector and civil society to discuss global health challenges and policy priorities. Ghana’s intervention adds to its advocacy for a more equitable global health system in which countries have greater influence over the policies and partnerships shaping their healthcare systems. At the same summit, President Mahama was honoured for his “outstanding leadership and commitment to advancing global health”. Health Minister Akandoh received the recognition on the President’s behalf.

items.title: Gouvernement : Fatima Zahra Mansouri scelle une majorité à quatre avec le PAM, l’Istiqlal, l’USFP et le PPS
items.description: Après deux rounds de consultations politiques, la cheffe du gouvernement désignée, Fatima-Zahra Mansouri, a tranché. Le Parti authenticité et modernité (PAM), arrivé en tête des législatives du 23 septembre, formera la prochaine majorité avec l’Istiqlal, l’Union socialiste des forces populaires (USFP) et le Parti du Progrès et du Socialisme (PPS). La coalition compte 207 députés sur 395 à la Chambre des représentants, soit neuf sièges au-dessus du seuil de la majorité absolue. L'annonce a été faite dans un communiqué conjoint publié ce lundi 12 octobre, faisant état officiellement l’accord conclu entre les quatre formations après deux séries de consultations. Le choix arrêté repose, selon le document, sur la volonté de constituer une majorité « politique » , cohérente dans ses orientations et capable de faire face aux défis auxquels le Maroc est confronté, aussi bien sur le plan intérieur qu’international. La configuration retenue donne au PAM le rôle de force centrale autour de laquelle s’organise la nouvelle majorité, tout en associant trois formations qui constituent le cœur de l’ancienne Koutla politique. Mais le choix de cette architecture ne relève pas seulement d’un calcul arithmétique. Le communiqué conjoint insiste sur les convergences politiques entre les quatre composantes et sur leur volonté commune de porter une même vision réformatrice. L’objectif affiché est de disposer d’une majorité capable d’accompagner les orientations royales en matière de construction démocratique, de bonne gouvernance, de justice sociale, d’équité territoriale et de renforcement des capacités productives de l’économie nationale. Cette architecture doit également permettre de répondre aux enjeux internes et aux contraintes extérieures auxquels le Maroc est confronté. Le choix des ministres, prochaine étape L’accord politique sur la majorité ouvre désormais la voie à la phase de composition de l’Exécutif. Les quatre partis doivent proposer des noms de ministres répondant à plusieurs critères fixés dans le communiqué : compétence, sens politique, intégrité et probité. L’objectif est de parvenir à une équipe gouvernementale homogène, capable de mettre en œuvre le futur programme gouvernemental. Un programme à élaborer rapidement La prochaine étape portera ainsi sur la préparation du programme gouvernemental et sur la finalisation de la composition de l’équipe ministérielle. Fatima-Zahra Mansouri affiche la volonté d’avancer rapidement, en demandant aux quatre composantes de la majorité de travailler à l’élaboration du programme qui devra traduire les priorités de la nouvelle coalition. The post Gouvernement : Fatima Zahra Mansouri scelle une majorité à quatre avec le PAM, l’Istiqlal, l’USFP et le PPS appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: US Open champion Zverev to become tennis world number one
items.description: Men’s tennis confirmed it will crown a new world number one as Germany’s Alexander Zverev was ensured the year-end honour on Monday after Carlos Alcaraz lost his third-round match in Shanghai. The career-first will cap a stellar season for the 29-year-old, the current world number two, after he won the French Open in June and the US Open in September. The French Open was his first-ever Grand Slam title. “It’s been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true,” Zverev said in a statement shared by the ATP Tour website. “So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury,” Zverev added. He suffered a career-threatening ankle injury in his French Open semi-final in 2022. Zverev will be the first German male player to finish his season as top-ranked in the world, and the oldest to lift the trophy, set to be presented in November, for the first time. Germany’s Angelique Kerber and Steffi Graf have both been the year-end number one women’s tennis player. Zverev’s achievement comes in a year where the previous two players to hold the top ranking, Italy’s Jannik Sinner and Spain’s Alcaraz, have skipped months of competition due to injury. Sinner, the current number one, has not competed since Wimbledon where he beat Zverev in the final. He announced last week his season was over due to a knee injury. Alcaraz, ranked third, was sidelined for months with a wrist injury from April until the US Open. Zverev, 6-foot-6 (1.98m), had been destined for the top from a young age, hailing from a tennis family where his mother and father both played the sport to a high level in the former Soviet Union. But he plays in the shadow of domestic violence allegations made by two former partners, which he has strenuously denied. The ATP Tour investigated one claim and found insufficient evidence to punish Zverev. Another led to a 2023 penalty order and fine from a German court which later dropped the case after a settlement was agreed in June of 2024 — hours before he was due to play in the French Open semi-finals. AFP The post US Open champion Zverev to become tennis world number one appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mahama honoured at 2026 World Health Summit in Berlin for global health leadership
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has been honoured at the 2026 World Health Summit in Berlin, Germany, for what organisers described as his “outstanding leadership and commitment to advancing global health”. The award, a Berliner Bär bearing the World Health Summit insignia, was presented to Ghana’s Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, who received it on the President’s behalf. The accompanying plaque read: “To His Excellency John Dramani Mahama, President of the Republic of Ghana, in recognition of his outstanding leadership and commitment to advancing global health.” The presenter, identified as Axel, asked the minister to convey the organisers’ greetings to the President. In his address at the summit, Mr Akandoh called for a global health system in which countries have a stronger role in shaping priorities and decisions affecting their populations. “Tonight, and over the past two days, we’ve heard the hard truth, the bold ideas, and the powerful voices. But one question stands above all others: Who gets to shape the future of global health?” he asked. “And the answer from Ghana is a clear one. Global health must not be designed for countries; it must be designed with countries and led by countries.” The minister said the position reflected President Mahama’s earlier address in Accra, which he described as a call to move “from dependency to dignity, from fragmentation to solidarity, from the promises of partnership to shared leadership”. Mr Akandoh also outlined initiatives he said reflected Ghana’s commitment to strengthening its health system. He cited the establishment of free primary healthcare, the Mahama Cares programme, increased investment in immunisation and efforts to mobilise domestic resources. “Resilience is not imported, and it is not donated. It must be built at home,” he said. He urged summit participants to work together to improve health outcomes and save lives. “At this point, I want to call up all of you from Accra to Jakarta to Berlin; let us all come together to reset to save more lives,” he said. The World Health Summit brings together participants from government, science, the private sector and civil society to discuss global health priorities and cooperation. Mahama’s recognition comes as Ghana advocates for a more equitable global health system, with countries having greater influence over health policies, financing and programmes affecting their populations. In his remarks, Mr Akandoh linked that objective to stronger domestic investment and international cooperation, arguing that resilient health systems must be built within countries rather than rely solely on external support.
